claims.text: A conventional elemental Cr coating is applied to zirconium-alloy cladding by physical vapor deposition.
The intervention is an approximately 10 nm Al2O3 interlayer deposited by atomic layer deposition directly between the Zr-alloy substrate and Cr coating.
ALD will produce a continuous, conformal Al2O3 interlayer in this coating system.
The Al2O3 interlayer is chemically inert and kinetically sluggish under the proposed conditions.
The Al2O3 interlayer inhibits atomic diffusion of Cr into Zr.
Slowing Cr–Zr interdiffusion minimizes formation of deleterious intermetallic compounds or mixed oxide phases at the interface.
Minimizing interfacial reaction products maintains the protective properties of the Cr coating.
Relative to Cr-coated cladding without a barrier, the Al2O3-containing system will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion during steam exposure at approximately 850°C for 10–60 minutes.
Reduced interdiffusion will prevent premature failure of the Cr coating during the specified high-temperature steam exposure.
The Al2O3-containing coating will retain protective performance during extended exposure to subcritical water at approximately 350°C.
The claimed operating boundary is approximately 350°C subcritical water for an unspecified extended duration.
The claimed accident boundary is approximately 850°C steam for 10–60 minutes.
The optimal Al2O3 thickness and its effects on adhesion and residual stress have not been determined.
Long-term durability under cyclic thermal and corrosion conditions remains undetermined.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says the interlayer will prevent Cr–Zr interdiffusion, whereas the mechanism allows either halting or merely slowing it and the predicted outcome claims only reduced interdiffusion. These statements differ in the asserted degree of suppression.
